Keywords: Kasha grain water fuel and shares
RagShortTexts: Water, fuel and cookware determine its preparation and distribution.

Variants.Content: Kasha uses available grain, with thickness and additions shaped by stores and means. Cooking needs vessels, fuel, water and tending; a bag of grain in camp is not yet a hot meal for everyone.
Cooking requires water and fire parties as others guard. Hasty departure wastes uncooked grain; the rear needs time to receive its meal too.
Ration accounts need cookware and cooks as well as stored grain. Feast additions without a regular source are a poor basis for daily supply planning.
Households balance porridge against seed and dues and fuel for each pot. Thinner food reaches more bowls without creating additional grain.
